text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins missed nine games to injury and has made up for lost time: 11 points in his 11 games, seven on the power play. Along the way he passed Kevin Lowe on Nov. 3 to become the Oilers' all-time leader in games played, now 1,042, all in Edmonton since going first overall in 2011. Then a puck to the face cut short his night against Vancouver on Nov. 7 after 6:36; the Edmonton Journal reported he'd wear a bubble, and he was back two nights later.

The pace won't hold at this level. He's shooting 22.2% against a talent range closer to 14%, and his team has scored 4.6 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. At five on five, Edmonton has had 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there.

Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming from the power play, and that's still where he earns his points. Watch his even-strength minutes as the Oilers get healthier.
headline: Nugent-Hopkins is back, and producing
